$comment: Every external fact Dev-OS depends on, with the source and the date it was checked. The smoke test makes this binding: the CLI may not wire a hook event, emit a subagent frontmatter key, or use an OpenCode plugin hook that is not recorded here. scripts/check-conformance.js verifies that offline; with --fetch (CI only) it re-reads the doc pages and reports drift. The CLI itself never fetches.

claude.name: Claude Code

docs.covers: hook events, per-event payloads and output contracts
subagent frontmatter keys and allowed values

verifiedAgainstBinary.note: the hook event enum and the hook dispatchers were read out of the installed binary, not only the docs

claude.blocking: exit 2 with the reason on stderr; some events also take a JSON decision
claude.contextOutput: plain stdout on SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit; hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext elsewhere

facts.claim: A PreCompact hook that exits 0 has its stdout used as the compaction summary instructions, capped at 10,000 characters per hook.
PostCompact has no decision control and cannot inject context; its stdout is discarded. SessionStart fires again after compaction, which is what re-injects context.
InstructionsLoaded fires once per instruction file with file_path, memory_type and load_reason. There is no instruction_files array.
A subagent with a memory scope automatically gains the Read, Write and Edit tools, which widens any tools: allowlist. No Dev-OS persona sets memory:.
Claude Code reads skills from .claude/skills only, which is why Dev-OS writes links there.
An identical handler in two settings files runs once, but a plugin's copy stays separate and runs in parallel; hence the plugin stand-down gate.

codex.name: Codex

docs.covers: hook config schema, events, payloads, trust model

codex.schemaShape: nested matcher groups, identical to Claude Code
codex.blocking: exit 2 with stderr, or permissionDecision deny

facts.claim: Project hooks do not run until the human trusts them with /hooks, and trust is tied to each script's hash, so a devos update requires re-trusting.
SessionEnd and Interrupt default to a 1 second timeout and allow at most 3.
PreToolUse cannot intercept hosted tools such as WebSearch; the docs call tool hooks a guardrail, not an enforcement boundary.
The skill list is capped at 2% of the context window, or 8,000 characters when the window is unknown.
Codex scans .agents/skills from the cwd up to the repo root. NOT re-verified live: no Codex CLI is installed here, and the equivalent claim for OpenCode proved wrong when measured.

Codex documents permissionDecision "ask" as not yet supported, so the Claude Code commit-approval prompt has no equivalent. Commit policy agent stays Claude-Code-only and the agent commit path is refused on other harnesses.

cursor.name: Cursor

docs.covers: hook config schema, event list, payloads, exit codes

cursor.schemaShape: flat handler lists under each camelCase event, with a required integer "version"

facts.claim: hooks.json requires a positive integer "version" field.
On preToolUse, permission "ask" is accepted but not enforced; only beforeShellExecution honours ask.
Project hooks require the workspace to be trusted.
Cursor scans .agents/skills plus .cursor/skills and .claude/skills. NOT re-verified live: Cursor is installed as an app only, with no CLI to measure.

beforeSubmitPrompt outputs only {continue, user_message}; it has no additional_context, so the per-turn Orchestrator directive cannot be injected there. Dev-OS does not wire it and relies on sessionStart instead.
Any exit code other than 2 (a crash, a timeout, a missing script) lets the action proceed unless the handler sets failClosed. Dev-OS sets failClosed on preToolUse.

preToolUse fires for every tool type including Read and Grep, and takes no matcher in the flat schema Dev-OS writes. The file gates therefore have to decide for themselves whether a tool writes the path it names.

antigravity.name: Antigravity CLI

docs.covers: hook config locations, schema, events, payloads, output

antigravity.schemaShape: a named bundle with "enabled"; lifecycle handlers sit directly under the event key, tool events use matcher groups
antigravity.blocking: a required {"decision":"deny"} with a reason; exit 2 is NOT documented as a denial

facts.claim: Antigravity CLI replaced Gemini CLI on 2026-06-18, so Dev-OS writes no .gemini/settings.json hooks.
Workspace hooks live at .agents/hooks.json at the project root, a file beside Dev-OS's own .agents/hooks/ script directory. Hooks in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json are not loaded.
Payload fields are camelCase and differ from every other harness: conversationId, workspacePaths, transcriptPath, artifactDirectoryPath, modelName, lastUserInput.

Tool ARGUMENTS are PascalCase, not just the envelope: run_command takes CommandLine, and the write tools take TargetFile plus CodeContent/ReplacementContent/ReplacementChunks. Folding only the outer field names left tool_input.command empty, which silently disabled every gate on this harness.
PreToolUse requires a "decision"; allow, auto_approve, deny, ask, force_ask and deny_unless_prior_grant are the documented values. Dev-OS answers allow on a permitted call and deny on a refusal.

OPEN QUESTION. The docs contradict themselves on the inject-step shape: the SessionStart example nests {"systemMessage": {"systemMessage": "..."}} while the PreInvocation field table shows a step as {"systemMessage": "text", "metadata": {...}} with a plain string. Dev-OS emits the plain string form, which matches the field table. If the nested form is real, session context is silently dropped on this harness. Needs measuring on a machine with the CLI.
The docs say nothing about a non-zero exit, empty stdout, invalid JSON or a hook timeout. Dev-OS therefore never relies on an exit code here: every refusal prints a deny decision.

opencode.name: OpenCode

docs.covers: plugin discovery directories only; the plugin API pages 404

verifiedAgainstTypings.note: hook names and signatures were read from the installed typings because the API docs 404 and third-party sources contradict each other

opencode.schemaShape: a JS module exporting a Plugin function that returns a flat object of named hooks
opencode.blocking: throw from tool.execute.before; its output carries only args, so there is no decision field

facts.claim: permission.asked, session.created and session.compacted are NOT hooks. The real name is permission.ask; session lifecycle arrives through the generic event hook.
A plain .js file at .opencode/plugins/ is auto-discovered; opencode debug config lists it under "plugin".

Measured with opencode debug skill in an OpenCode install, NO project-level skills are discovered: not from .agents/skills, .claude/skills or .opencode/skills. Only built-ins and the global ~/.claude/skills are listed. This contradicts opencode.ai/docs/skills and is why the same doc-only claims for Codex and Cursor are marked suspect.
tool.execute.before fires for every tool, including the lowercase read/grep tools, so the file gates must distinguish writers from readers themselves.
